findings.title: Shard path now interpolates every target twice
findings.body: `runShardSplitQuery` interpolates each target with `datasource.applyTemplateVariables` here, then passes those already-interpolated targets as sub-requests into `runSplitQuery` (line 163). Since this PR, `runSplitQuery` also interpolates its targets (querySplitting.ts:299), so in the sharding path every target goes through `applyTemplateVariables`/`templateSrv.replace` twice. The updated test 'Interpolates queries before running' asserts `applyTemplateVariables` was called 5 times for a single query (1 here + 1 per each of the 4 shard sub-requests), which confirms the duplication; before this PR the shard path interpolated exactly once. A second replace pass over already-resolved text is usually a no-op, but it corrupts expressions whose interpolated values themselves contain `$name`/`${name}` sequences (e.g. a label value or regex containing `$`) and it doubles templating work. Guard against this, e.g. add an option so `runSplitQuery` skips interpolation when the caller already did it, or stop pre-interpolating in the shard path and expose the selector needed for `fetchLabelValues` another way.

findings.title: $__range splitting guard is untested after interpolation
findings.body: Interpolation now runs before the `partition(queries, (query) => !querySupportsSplitting(query))` split. `querySupportsSplitting` relies on `isQueryWithRangeVariable(query.expr)` to keep queries that use `$__range` out of splitting, precisely because `$__range` is supposed to be resolved from each query's time range. There is no test covering a `$__range` query after interpolation. If the datasource's `applyTemplateVariables` resolves `$__range`/`$__range_ms`/`$__range_s` from `request.scopedVars`, `isQueryWithRangeVariable` will no longer find the variable, the guard silently stops protecting the query, and it gets time-sliced with `$__range` computed per sub-range rather than for the full range. Add a test asserting a `$__range` query still lands in the non-splitting partition after interpolation.
